style: 3D animated (Pixar-style CG) for 0-58.00 s; hard cut to a 7-shot live-action handheld phone 'real me' tag 58.00-60.03 s (opens on the real creator and a real woman copying Mom's scream pose). Single-word white captions (bold condensed caps, black outline) at lower-middle; small white hook title 'MOM SAID I'D FAIL' + skull emoji in the first 1.3 s.
logline: Mom finds her son's $2,000 savings gone on clothes to resell - with only three sales. She gives him one week to make every dollar back. After a night of near-giving-up the orders flood in, Mom ends up packing boxes beside him, they share the win - and then she discovers a closet full of new inventory.

hook.mechanic: Door-burst confrontation: title 'MOM SAID I'D FAIL' as the bedroom door flies open and Mom storms in waving his empty wallet ('Nate! Where is all your money?'), a wallet slammed on the desk ('You had $2,000'), a fast chair spin ('I spent it'), and two whip-blur reveals of the stock. Money stakes with a number, a villain-of-the-moment and 7 shots in under 5 s.
hook.first_line: Nate! Where is all your money?

montage.description: Main montage, wordless grind (8.6 s, 8 shots): hands typing listings, a laptop filling with 'Order #1 Confirmed' notifications, fast-motion packing at the desk, a sealed poly-bag insert, 'Order #2 Confirmed', then a locked-off desk set-up with a wall clock where night -> golden sunrise -> night time-lapse and stacks of mailers rising beside him. A second, music-driven packing montage runs 42.10-49.33 (shots 30-48, 19 shots, many 0.08-0.25 s): the same frontal Mom-and-son two-shot at the packing table with the background and light swapped by match cuts (warm stock room, blue night, sunny palm-tree yard, warm brick wall), single-frame blue flashes, Mom kissing his cheek, and the shouted 'More!' / 'Keep packing!' / 'I am!'. Stats count both.

stats.dead_air: None in the audio sense: a music bed runs the full 60 s (silencedetect at -35 dB/0.4 s found no silence). Gaps with no dialogue (>= 1.5 s): 14.89-17.15 (2.3 s), 19.79-28.55 (8.8 s), 36.97-39.46 (2.5 s), 41.94-47.20 (5.3 s), 53.29-55.95 (2.7 s), 57.18-60.03 (2.9 s).

beats.summary: HOOK: door bursts open, Mom with the empty wallet: 'Nate! Where is all your money?' - 'What?' - 'You had $2,000.' - 'I spent it.' - 'On what?' - 'My business.' Whip reveals of the stock.
Interrogation: 'You spent $2,000 on clothes?' - 'They're not just clothes.' - 'How many have you sold?' Phone insert: Sales 3. 'Three?' - 'Yes.' Mom's ECU snarl.
The deal: 'I'm gonna make it back.' - 'Then prove it.' - 'One week.' - 'Make your $2,000 back.' - 'All of it?' - 'Every dollar.' - 'Fine.' Nose-to-nose profile two-shot.
Low point: night, a bad notification, head down on his arms: 'I can't let her down.' He sits up: 'One more time.'
MONTAGE: listing, first orders confirmed, packing in fast motion, clock time-lapse through night and sunrise, stacks rising.
Breakthrough: 'Wait, wait, wait.' ECU on his eye, phone flooding with orders: 'Mom!' He runs to her door: 'Look!' - 'What am I looking at?' - 'Orders!' - 'How many?'

Scale: empty office fills with stock as he counts '10, 20, 30'. Packing table: 'Wait, they're still coming!' - 'Right now?' Mom grabs a shirt: 'Give me that... You're too slow.' His grin: 'Wait... OK!'
MONTAGE 2: mother and son packing side by side as the world swaps around them; 'More!' - 'Keep packing!' - 'I am!'
Payoff + button: boxes drop in, 'We did it.' - 'You did.' - 'No. We did.' The closet door swings open on a wall of boxes: 'Nate... Nate... more inventory?' Whip to Mom's screaming ECU.
Real-me tag: real creator and a real woman copy the scream pose in a stock room, then handheld flexes (dinner by the marina, Rolls-Royce, starlight interior, friends and cars, yacht).

transcription: faster-whisper 'small' (CPU, int8), word timestamps; dialogue windows re-run one by one (no VAD) and cross-checked against the burned-in word captions. Fixed from captions: 'Then prove it', the timing of 'Wait, wait, wait', 'Keep packing!' and 'Nate... Nate... more inventory?'. 'Nate!', 'Give me that', 'What?', 'You're too slow', 'Wait...', 'More!', 'I am!' were missed by the first pass and recovered on the re-run.
why_it_works: The hook puts a number on the stakes: an empty wallet and '$2,000' in the first 3 s, against a named doubter ('MOM SAID I'D FAIL').
Seven shots in under 5 s (door burst, wide reveal, wallet slam, chair spin, two whip reveals) - the energy of the edit sells the argument before the story starts.
Rapid ping-pong dialogue (2-4 word lines at 3+ words/s) with single-word captions plays like a sitcom; the 'Sales: 3' phone insert is the punchline.
A clear contract with a deadline ('One week... every dollar') gives the viewer a scoreboard to watch for the rest of the reel.
A real low point (head on arms, 'I can't let her down') before the montage makes the win feel earned and keeps it about the relationship, not just money.
Time and scale are shown visually: clock time-lapse through night and sunrise, stacks rising, an empty office filling as he counts '10, 20, 30'.
The second montage turns Mom from opponent into partner, with match-cut world swaps and a cheek kiss - the emotional payoff most viewers share.
'We did it' - 'You did' - 'No, we did' gives a warm resolution, then the closet reveal and screaming ECU flip it into a laugh for the button.
The live-action tag opens by copying the cartoon's last pose with a real person, tying the fable to real life ('based on a true story') before the lifestyle flex and loop.
undetermined: Music identity not identified (music bed under everything; only speech transcribed).
Speakers of 'Give me that', 'What?', and 'More!' inferred from mouths and context, not certain.
'Three, three...' (29.6 s) is as heard and captioned; its meaning in the story is unclear (possibly counting orders).
'Nate... Nate... more inventory?' text is from captions; whisper heard 'I'm sorry' / 'Well, more inventory', so exact wording and split timing are approximate.
Shot 49 (8.1 s) is counted as one shot: static two-shot to 54.2 s, then one continuous move to the closet profile; no cut found by eye or frame difference.
Montage 2 (shots 30-48) includes three 0.08 s blue 'flash' shots counted as cuts; their exact frames are approximate to +/- 1 frame.
Shots 16 and 23-25 use fast motion; jumps inside the same set-up are treated as speed ramps, not cuts.
Woman in the live-action tag is not identified (likely the creator's real mother, given the 'true story' caption; not confirmed).
